newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian PM expected to take over one month leave.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian PM expected to take over one month leave.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad is expected to take a holiday of more than a month, probably beginning in late May, a senior government source said on Wednesday.

The 71-year-old leader, who is on an official visit to African nations, could start the unusually long leave period at the end of May, the source said. Spokesmen for Mahathir could not be reached for comment.
"He is going on leave at the end of this month," the source said, adding that Mahathir could be gone for "more than a month".
Mahathir who keeps a full schedule, seldom takes holidays of longer than a few weeks. During his absence, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is expected to step in.
Mahathir's long leave raised questions among some political analysts about his health.
But the government source said: "This has nothing to do with his health."
Mahathir, who had a heart operation in 1989, has generally enjoyed good health.
Another government source said Mahathir was taking leave to finish writing a book and promote Malaysia's new technology zone, the Multimedia Super Corridor, overseas.
